sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vocabulary column no. 144 'North-east Ki-lega or Ba-lega' (= Kanu per Glottolog/Maho) is a comparative wordlist based on Griffith's 'Regga' list in Last 1885 p. 203 plus Johnston's own 1900 additions (p. 806); location note p. 495. The only prosodic remark is the blanket notation convention on p. 41: accent 'is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable than the penultimate' -- a general Bantu convention, not a statement about Kanu.
